reason: Alalu is the first holder of divine kingship in heaven; his nine-year reign and overthrow by Anu are the Hittite/Hurrian case study in sovereignty, succession, and the mandate of heaven.
The 'Kingship in Heaven' myth survives only in Hittite cuneiform tablets from Boğazköy-Hattusa (CTH 344), making Alalu a flagship patron of ancient Near Eastern archives and textual preservation.
Alalu's name and story are obscure outside Assyriological and Hittite scholarship; restoring him is exactly the kind of mythic recovery PuniCodex exists to perform.
His myth is a standard comparative example in courses on ancient Near Eastern religion, Indo-European succession mythology, and Hittite civilization.
